media_item.focus_or_theme: Coerced false confessions, juvenile suspects, DNA exoneration
media_item.summary_notes: The episode explores Jeffrey Deskovic's case, who falsely confessed after a lengthy interrogation as a teen and was exonerated by DNA after 16 years. The case highlights conviction despite pre-trial DNA exclusion and is a prominent example of a coerced false confession from a juvenile, despite exculpatory DNA evidence.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Explores Deskovic falsely confessing after lengthy interrogation as a teen; Exonerated by DNA after 16 years; Established foundation. Available via ABC.
research_notes_other.research_findings: While a specific 20/20 episode titled "Confession at Gunpoint" wasn't confirmed, the details of Jeffrey Deskovic's case match the description perfectly. His case is a prominent example of a coerced false confession from a juvenile, despite exculpatory DNA evidence being available even before trial.

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Rape and Murder (of 15-year-old classmate Angela Correa in 1989)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Jeffrey Deskovic was wrongfully convicted of rape and murder in 1990. He was interrogated at 16 for over 6 hours without a parent or lawyer and coerced into a false confession. He was exonerated by DNA evidence in 2006 after serving nearly 16 years.
contributing_factors_raw: Coerced false confession (interrogated at 16 for 6+ hours, polygraphs, no parent/lawyer)
